body_markdown:
*Welcome to our monthly market report, where we sum up the previous month’s activity in the collector car market with charts and key talking points using the data we gather every day.*


## Key Takeaways


- The[Hagerty Market Rating](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/how-the-hagerty-market-rating-works/) , which measures the status of the collector car market in terms of activity or “heat,” is essentially flat from the previous month, dropping -0.01 to 58.73. Changes in the Market Rating have been minimal for most of the year despite large swings in certain segments. (The Market Rating measures the market as a whole, and any rating between 50 and 60 is still considered “flat market” territory.)
- Monterey Car Week dominated the headlines and made up a large chunk of the numbers in August. The auction calendar was still full in September, however, with new auctions from Barrett-Jackson and RM Sotheby’s, plus a revived Fall Auburn auction from Kruse helping to push September volume up 41% compared to 2025.
- The average sale price is up 30% year-over-year while median sale price is up 7%. These metrics have been moving apart for much of the year, but moved slightly closer to each other in September as more mid-market live auctions took place.
- Buying a seven-figure car in an online auction is now mainstream. A dozen cars sold for more than $1M online in September vs. eight at a live venue.
- Vehicles from the 1990s and later continue to move the market. Through the first nine months of 2025, they represented 53% of the lot offered. In 2026, volume has inched up 2 percentage points, and dollar share has grown by 8 percentage points.
- Ferraris continue to move the market. Of the more than $1.6B year-over-year increase in global auction sales volume, Ferraris account for nearly half ($730M).
- Due to strength at the top of the market, consignors have been more willing to run cars at no reserve. Only 70% of cars at the $1M+ level are carrying a reserve, compared to 84% at this time last year.


Simon Gosselin/RM Sotheby's
